tools.name: list_crawls
tools.description: Recent crawls in this Toadstone, newest first: id, URL, status and page counts. Start here when you do not have a crawl id.

status.description: Only crawls in this state, e.g. 'completed' or 'running'.

tools.name: crawl_status
tools.description: Progress of one crawl: status, pages done, pages found and an ETA. Poll this after start_crawl.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id, as list_crawls reports it.

tools.name: start_crawl
tools.description: Start a crawl and return its id. Writes, so it is refused unless this server was started with writes enabled, and the target host must be on the allow-list.

url.description: The http(s) URL to start from.

render.description: Render with a headless browser. Much slower; needed for JS-built pages.

max_urls.description: Stop after this many URLs. Defaults to the server cap, and may not exceed it.

max_depth.description: Maximum click depth from the start URL.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: Issues from one crawl, filterable by severity, check, category and URL prefix, with a tally by severity and by check. Each issue carries its stable id, its evidence and how to fix it.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id, as list_crawls reports it.

check.description: Check slug, e.g. 'missing_meta_description'; comma-separate for several.

since_crawl.description: Only issues new since this crawl id.

tools.name: issue_detail
tools.description: One issue by its stable id, with a summary of the page it was found on. The crawl id is required: an issue id is stable across crawls, so it alone does not identify one row.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id, as list_crawls reports it.

tools.name: page_detail
tools.description: Everything known about one URL in one crawl: the stored row, its issues, inbound and outbound links, and how it changed against the previous crawl of the site.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id, as list_crawls reports it.

url.description: The exact URL, as the crawl stored it.

baseline.description: Crawl id to diff against. Defaults to the previous crawl of this domain.

include_links.description: Include link rows, not just counts (default true).

tools.name: regression_diff
tools.description: What changed between two crawls: issues that are new, fixed, and still open, matched by stable issue id.

tools.name: export_dataset
tools.description: Export one dataset from a crawl as text. Datasets: issues, pages, links, graph-nodes, graph-edges, sitemap-files, sitemap-coverage, duplicates, redirects, broken-links, headings, images. Formats: csv, json, ndjson (xlsx and zip are downloads, not MCP results).

crawl_id.description: A crawl id, as list_crawls reports it.

limit.description: Rows to keep, for csv and ndjson.

severity.description: Filter, where the dataset has a severity column.

check.description: Filter, where the dataset has a check column.

url_prefix.description: Only rows whose URL starts with this.

status_code.description: Only rows with this HTTP status.

tools.name: check_reference
tools.description: What a check means, how severe it is and how to fix it. With no argument, the whole reference for this install.

tools.name: accept_issue
tools.description: Mute one issue with a reason, so it stops being reported as open. Writes, so it is refused on a read-only server.

base_domain.description: Scope the acceptance to one domain.

result.instructions:
Toadstone is an SEO crawler. Crawls have numeric ids; issues have ids that are stable across crawls, so the same defect keeps its id until it is fixed.

Start with list_crawls to find a crawl id, then list_issues for what is wrong, page_detail for one URL, and regression_diff to compare two crawls. check_reference explains any check slug.

Guardrails: read-write; crawls allowed against localhost; at most 100 URLs per crawl.

result.instructions:
Toadstone is an SEO crawler. Crawls have numeric ids; issues have ids that are stable across crawls, so the same defect keeps its id until it is fixed.

Start with list_crawls to find a crawl id, then list_issues for what is wrong, page_detail for one URL, and regression_diff to compare two crawls. check_reference explains any check slug.

Guardrails: read-only; crawls allowed against only hosts already crawled in this install; at most 2000 URLs per crawl.
